Commentary.Commentary: WE ARE BACK!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Zimbabwe were looking disheartened with the way Bangladesh were playing in the first half of the innings. They were looking a bit tired and confused as to how much more they'd concede but Luke Jongwe came in with some fresh air to strike twice in the over and that turned out to be the moment of the match. Since then Zimbabwe didn't look back and pulled things back in style. A completely different kind of attitude in the next 10 overs has resulted in Zimbabwe finishing strong. The tourists have a chance to get a win here. The bowlers have done a good job. Can the batters finish things off?

A tale of two halves - Bangladesh scored 100 runs at the halfway mark with both the openers bossing the game. Tanzid Hasan and Soumya Sarkar were scoring at 10 runs per over. It felt like today Bangladesh would cross the 200 mark but there was a twist in fortunes as they lost 10 wickets while adding just 43 runs on the board. A downfall no one saw coming. Hasan scored a fine fifty but Sarkar followed him in the same over and since then the wickets kept on falling.
OUT! GONE! Short in length and on leg. Rahman makes room and tries to slash it away but edges it to the keeper who makes no mistake. Bangladesh finish with 143 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. The players are out in the middle. Sikandar Raza is sharing some final key words. Soumya Sarkar and Tanzid Hasan to open for Bangladesh.Spin to start, Sikandar Raza to bowl.

Najmul Hossain Shanto says they are happy to bat first. Shares Shakib Al Hasan, Soumya Sarkar and Mustafizur Rahman are in the team. Tells they want to focus on the death bowling and bat well in these two matches.

Sikandar Raza says they'll bowl first, it is a typical Dhaka wicket and hopes to make early inroads. Informs about the team changes. Shares they are going through a rebuilding process and there will be mistakes.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tadiwanashe Marumani, Brian Bennett, Sikandar Raza (C), Clive Madande (WK), Ryan Burl, Johnathan Campbell, Faraz Akram, Luke Jongwe, Wellington Masakadza, Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Soumya Sarkar, Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Towhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali( WK), Shakib Al Hasan, Tanvir Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.
Toss - Zimbabwe have won the toss and will bowl.

Hello and welcome to the fourth game between Zimbabwe and Bangladesh. The home team have shown sheer dominance so far winning all the games and clinching the series as well. They have done well so far and will look to clean sweep against Zimbabwe eho are lacking a bit in all three departments. The form of some of the experienced players is worrisome. Zimbabwe are yet to show their full potential and will hope to put on a side in this game with nothing to lose much. Let's hope we have a cracker of a game. Stay tuned.
...Match Day...

We are awaiting the 4th T20I between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe at the Shere Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur. It has all been the dominance of Bangladesh in the first three games. With two games left, they will hope to whitewash the visitors and gain some momentum before the T20I World Cup in the coming month. The form of Litton Das will be a big concern for the team but their middle order looks strong. In the last game, Towhid Hridoy and Jaker Ali put up a strong stand to stabilize the innings but their lower middle order couldn't give an explosive end. Their bowling unit took up responsibility and put the opposition under pressure from the start of the innings. Mohammad Saifuddin ended up with three wickets while Rishad Hossain earned two. The rest of the pack got one wicket each to win the game by 9 runs. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, have come close to winning but haven't been able to cross the final step. They will want to win the remaining games and gain some confidence. Blessing Muzarabani has been their star bowler and impressed once again with his three wickets in the 3rd T20I. Sikandar Raza and Faraz Akram got one each. The others will need to make sure that they break partnerships in regular intervals and keep the pressure on the batters. Their batters also need to preserve their wickets, especially their openers who are expected to give a strong start. Tadiwanashe Marumani, Johnathan Campbell, and Faraz Akram were the only batters to cross the 20-run mark which looks troublesome for the squad. There are a lot of things to work on for them. Which team are you supporting?
